title: Manager: deletion decided by code (superseded branches deleted; file deletions checked at merge; git clean refused)
item: After a task merges, the manager deletes that task's earlier attempt branches when a script confirms they are superseded, and records each deleted branch's name and last commit id in the run report
motivation: The manager may delete a merged task's branches only with git branch -d, which refuses a branch whose commits are not on the working branch. A retry copies the earlier work onto a fresh branch as a new commit, so the earlier attempts never count as merged and the owner deletes them by hand. It happened for every task that needed a retry: 28 and 36 on 2026-11-15, 49 on 2026-11-17. Whether a branch is superseded is a mechanical question, and by the owner's rule a mechanical check uses code.
notes: A branch is superseded when all three hold: its name is task/<id> or task/<id>-<n>; task <id> is Done on the working branch and its merge commit is on the working branch; the branch is not checked out in any worktree. A script in scripts/checks.py decides this; only then may the manager run git branch -D on it. The run report lists each deleted branch with its last commit id, so it can be restored with git branch <name> <id> while git still holds the commit. Branches of a task that is not Done, and any branch not named for a task, are never deleted. Deleted by hand on 2026-11-17 on the owner's word, for the record: task/049 at 6ad8b8d and task/049-2 at b637e68. When a task branch is left over and the script does not confirm it (so the manager may not delete it), the run report must make the case itself, so the owner does not have to ask elsewhere: for each such branch, which of the three conditions failed, how many files differ from the working branch and how many exist only on the branch, and a recommendation to delete or keep with its reason. On 2026-11-17 the report said only that two branches 'are superseded and can be deleted'; the owner had to get the evidence from Claude in chat. Two more mechanisms, approved by the owner on 2026-11-17, for the DECISIONS.md rule 'an agent proposes and does not delete'. (a) A check at merge time, for files git tracks: checks.py protected fails a task branch that deletes or renames a file which existed on the working branch at the fork point, unless the task names that path in a new optional owner's field, may_delete (a list of paths, like may_edit). This reads git's own record of the change, so it does not depend on which command did the deleting. A file the branch itself added may be deleted or renamed freely. (b) A hook, for what git cannot restore: while a run is active the PreToolUse hook also refuses a Bash command whose text runs `git clean`, or `git branch -D` / `git branch --delete --force` outside the manager's own cleanup step. Like the push hook it reads command text, so it is an early stop, not proof. Do not try to block `rm`: builders delete their own temporary files, and a text match on rm is easy to get around.
done_means: A checks.py command takes a branch name and exits 0 only when the three conditions in the notes hold. commands/manage.md and SKILL.md say the manager deletes a branch with git branch -D only after that command passes, and writes the branch's name and last commit id in the run report. Tests in temporary git repos cover: an earlier attempt of a Done task (deleted), a branch of a task that is not Done (kept), a checked-out branch (kept), a branch not named for a task (kept). For a leftover task branch the command does not confirm, the run report states which condition failed, the count of files that differ from the working branch and of files only on the branch, and a recommendation with its reason. checks.py protected fails a branch that deletes or renames a file present at the fork point and not named in may_delete, and passes when the path is named or the branch itself added the file; tasks.py lint accepts may_delete as a list of paths; tests cover each case. While a run is active the hook refuses `git clean` and a forced branch deletion, and allows the manager's cleanup step; tests cover both. The manager tests pass, all of them.
draft_note: Drafted by Claude in chat on 2026-11-17 on the owner's yes; the two deletion mechanisms added the same day on his yes. Hard dependencies on tasks 57 and 37 because all three change the same manager files. Set to Ready on 2026-11-17 on the owner's instruction.

decided_for_you.chosen: RULING: FAILS on line (1), advisor job c, tasks/advice/058-1.md: the hook skipped any quoted -m message, so a command substitution inside one passed; sent back to one fresh builder (d257edb)
decided_for_you.would_change: If running the hook on the two commands it names returned exit 2, or you say a text hook need not see a substitution inside a commit message

decided_for_you.chosen: RULING: HOLDS on line (1) after the fix, advisor job c, tasks/advice/058-2.md. Known holes left, all needing -m inside another quoting context: echo ' -m "' ; <refused command> ; echo '"', bash -c with a single-quoted message inside double quotes, and bash -cm
decided_for_you.would_change: A command that hides a refused git call at the top level; or you want the hook to be proof rather than an early stop

decided_for_you.chosen: Builder: the hook allows a forced deletion only when checks.py superseded passes for every branch named, so a builder could also delete a superseded branch (builder.md still forbids it)
decided_for_you.rejected: Recognising a fixed command form or a flag the manager sets
decided_for_you.would_change: If builders must not delete even a superseded branch

decided_for_you.chosen: Builder: every clean form is refused, -n included; superseded counts files tip to tip; the full commit id is printed for restore
decided_for_you.rejected: Letting -n through; counting from the fork point; the short id

decided_for_you.chosen: Retry builder: a heredoc commit message is refused; a single-quoted message is always skipped; a double-quoted one only without a backtick or $(; step 7 commits the merge with a plain quoted -m, or -F when the title holds a backtick or $(
decided_for_you.rejected: Treating a quoted-delimiter heredoc as inert (cat <<'EOF' | sh runs it)
decided_for_you.would_change: If builders often commit heredoc messages naming these commands and refusals cost too much
